Low-biomass samples (biopsies, swabs, blood, ascitic fluid) carry so little
bacterial DNA that contamination from reagents and the lab can make up a
large share of the sequencing reads. This project evaluates how well
contaminant-removal methods work, using data where the right answer is known.

| Part | Question | |
|---|---|---|
| **1. Benchmark** | How do decontam and simple filters perform on a real mock-community dilution series? | [Read](analysis/01_mock_dilution_benchmark.html) |
| **2. Simulation** | How do the number of negative controls, DNA quantification and cross-contamination change the answer? | [Read](analysis/02_simulation_study.html) |
| **3. Guide** | Which method and threshold should I use, and how do I report it? | [Read](analysis/03_decision_guide.html) |

Code, data and tests: [github.com/joangordo/decontam-low-biomass](https://github.com/joangordo/decontam-low-biomass)
